sourceBaseline.interpretation: The source ranking query and both colliding core baseline definitions are pinned as compatibility evidence only. Generated-schema and Diesel-filter omissions, missing LOWER(wallet_address) functional indexing, adopted schema, query plan and reconciliation remain STOPs.

targetBase.interpretation: Immutable completed post-A2.7 snapshot before extracting the raw repository contract and adding the unwired core adapter.

invariants.claim: The PostgreSQL adapter is physically owned by the backend core repository layer that owns plan, assignment and permission storage.
One schema-qualified read-only Diesel SQL statement with one wallet bind returns the complete raw observation.
The observation instant comes from statement_timestamp() in the same statement and is represented as Unix epoch microseconds.
LEFT JOIN rows preserve raw inactive, expired, missing-plan, permission-active and unrelated permission facts without SQL-side entitlement filtering.
A clean sentinel row represents a successful empty owner snapshot without inventing an assignment or conflating it with repository failure.
Pure decoding rejects contradictory row shapes, mixed wallet or observation facts and conflicting duplicates as corrupt repository data.
Equivalent duplicate rows are idempotent and assignment and permission output order is deterministic.
The raw snapshot DTO, repository error and repository port live in epsx-contracts without SQL, clock or ranking decision policy.
Ranking entitlement resolution remains in the identity crate and consumes the owner-neutral shared repository contract.
Identity runtime fails closed until an authenticated entitlement adapter is wired; it does not construct, authorize or invoke the extracted store.
A2.8 adds no migration, schema regeneration, runtime configuration or database adoption claim.
All evidence is local static inspection and exact hermetic tests and authorizes no database, network, listener, browser, deployment or production action.

residualStops.claim: The statement and decoder have not been exercised against PostgreSQL; static inspection is not database compatibility evidence.
No catalog or migration-ledger proof identifies either pinned baseline as the schema adopted by a populated environment.
The v5 and v6 source migration directories share one Diesel migration version and their coexistence remains unresolved.
Generated primary schema and Diesel table filtering omit wallet_plan_assignments; A2.8 neither regenerates nor certifies them.
Neither pinned baseline proves a functional index matching LOWER(wallet_address), and A2.8 adds no migration.
The complete raw join is intentionally unbounded and has no representative EXPLAIN, cardinality ceiling, latency budget or load evidence.
Transaction isolation, MVCC behavior and snapshot consistency under concurrent plan or permission writes remain unproved.
Synthetic row fixtures and static SQL inspection do not reconcile target results with populated source authority data.
Identity runtime rejects ranking authority requests until the authenticated entitlement adapter is wired; no store activation or production ranking authority is claimed.
Identity RPC still lacks workload identity, exact caller authorization, owner binding and TLS policy.
Ranking changes still have no transactional outbox, monotonic revision, durable cursor, replay or gap repair.
No typed BFF or Dioxus UI consumes this adapter and no loading, free, paid, stale or error browser flow is proven.
Route ownership, runtime configuration, images, gateway, Kubernetes, canary, rollback and deployment remain unchanged.
Passing A2.8 integrity never authorizes a database, service, secret, network, deployment or production action.

requiredExecutionOrder: E01 freeze the source query, both colliding baselines, generated-schema gap and immutable post-A2.7 target base
E02 extract only the owner-neutral snapshot DTO, repository error and repository port into epsx-contracts
E03 add one physically core-owned, schema-qualified, read-only raw snapshot statement
E04 decode sentinel, assignment, plan and permission rows strictly with deterministic grouping
E05 replay only the frozen row ledger and SQL-shape checks through exact offline tests
E06 certify adopted schema, migration ledger and the LOWER(wallet_address) index decision separately
E07 measure representative query plans, cardinality, concurrency and latency before activation
E08 reconcile populated source authority and resolve lifecycle and alternate-entitlement policy
E09 wire an authenticated identity runtime plus durable revision and recovery semantics
E10 obtain separate UI, staging, canary, rollback and production deployment authorization
